posts.title: Unlocking Our Collective Impact: Why Rotary Club Central Matters More Than Ever
posts.description: AI Generated infographic based on this write up As Rotarians, our passion for service drives everything we do. From local hands-on projects to global health campaigns, we give our time, energy, and hearts to being People of Action. But how do we track the real reach of our hard work? And how do we make sure our goals aren't just wishful thinking, but clear milestones we actually hit? The answer is right at our fingertips: Rotary Club Central (RCC). Far from being a boring administrative chore or a digital dumping ground, Rotary Club Central is the real engine behind our clubs, our Distirct, and indeed Rotary International. Whether you’re a club president, a committee chair, or a dedicated member, RCC is the tool that turns our shared vision into measurable progress. The Power of RCC for Your Club 1. posts.title: Why are there Silly Fines at Rotary meetings?
posts.description: Photo credit: Unsplash Silly fines, as the name suggests are fines that members are charged at a meeting to help the club run its operations and projects. They are meant to make members laugh and have fun while the fines are being paid. Silly fines are not supposed to be an instrument of punishment, where members are only fined for not doing something. Occasionally, members can be fined for not being appropriately 'dressed' as Rotarians (such as not wearing their pins). However that shouldn't be routine. A member can even be fined for being promoted at work, or looking radiant at a meeting. Another funny example can be fining bald members. 👨🏾 🦲 To ensure that members enjoy giving these tokens to help their clubs, some clubs have decided to scrap the "silly fine" name and rather take "happy dollar" or "gratitude dollar" where members pay a token for something they are happy about, or grateful for. posts.title: AngiLin FoodDrive donates to The Potters Village Orphange
posts.description: Group picture with the Founder and children of The Potters Village orphanage AngiLin FoodDrive, the humanitarian arm of AngiLin Catering Services visited the Potters Village Orphanage in Dodowa last Saturday, May 1, 2021 and shared love with them. The group was joined by Nessa's Candlelight Foundation and made a donation of food items, toiletries, stationery and nose masks to the orphanage to mark their mid-year donation programme. The leader of the team, Angela Agyeman mentioned that the donation was different than the usual exercise the group used to carry out, as it didn't include cooked food. The group plans to hold such mid-year donations in the coming years, and encourages others to come on board in giving back to society. Angela making the donation Items presented to the orphanage For over 3 years, AngiLin Catering Services has been organising food drives every December in suburbs of Accra.
